claim: Gravin protein is reduced 9.15-fold in seminoma tumor samples compared to adjacent normal tissue.
source: Surprisingly, immunoblot analysis of clinical samples from three seminoma patients detected a 9.15-fold reduction in Gravin protein compared to adjacent tissue (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data from clinical samples shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: Aurora A and Plk1 protein levels decrease in seminoma samples that show Gravin reduction.
source: Interestingly, the loss of Gravin was accompanied by a decrease in two essential cell cycle regulator kinases, Aurora A and Plk1 (Figure 1A, mid panels, and Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data from clinical samples shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: Gravin signal intensity per mitotic cell is reduced 4.88-fold in seminoma sections compared to normal testis.
source: Moreover, counterstaining with the mitotic marker phospho-Ser 10-Histone 3B (p-H3B) indicated that a 4.88-fold decrease in Gravin was observed in mitotic cells (Figure 1E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 1E-G.

claim: The mitotic index is elevated 3.78-fold in seminoma tissue compared to normal tissue.
source: The mitotic index was elevated in seminoma compared to normal tissue (3.78-fold, Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by mitotic index calculations from tissue sections shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Gravin knockout mice display a 3.39-fold increase in mitotic index in seminiferous tubules compared to wild-type mice.
source: Under these conditions, Gravin knockout mice displayed a 3.39-fold increase in the mitotic index compared to wild-type seminiferous tubule sections (Figure 1I–K).
evidence: The claim is supported by mitotic index measurements from mouse tissue sections shown in Figure 1I-K.

claim: Gravin knockout mice exhibit a 3.07-fold reduction in apoptotic cells in seminiferous tubules.
source: Gravin knockout mice also exhibited a 3.07-fold reduction in the number of cells undergoing apoptosis (TUNEL-positive cells; Figure 1L, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by TUNEL staining data from mouse tissue sections shown in Figure 1L.

claim: Gravin null MEFs display a slower rate of proliferation compared to wild-type MEFs.
source: In primary cultures of mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs), Gravin null cells displayed a slower rate of proliferation compared to wild type ([Akakura et al., 2010]; Figure 1—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: The claim is supported by growth curve data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and cited literature.

claim: Gravin null MEFs show increased senescent morphology compared to wild-type MEFs.
source: In primary cultures of mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs), Gravin null cells displayed a slower rate of proliferation compared to wild type ([Akakura et al., 2010]; Figure 1—figure supplement 1D) with a concomitant increase in senescent morphology (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by senescence scoring data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Gravin interacts with Aurora A kinase.
source: A key advance in our studies came with the discovery that Gravin also anchors an upstream mitotic kinase, Aurora A (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Aurora A and Plk1 are detected in Gravin immune complexes isolated from mitotic cell lysates.
source: To test this concept, four complementary approaches were used. First, immunoblot analysis detected Aurora A and Plk1 in Gravin immune complexes isolated from mitotic cell lysates (Figure 2A, lane 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and immunoblot data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Aurora B kinase does not interact with Gravin.
source: Control experiments confirmed that the closely related Aurora B kinase does not interact with Gravin (Figure 2B, lane 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The RII subunit of PKA constitutively interacts with Gravin throughout the cell cycle.
source: Conversely, the RII subunit of protein kinase A (PKA) constitutively interacts with Gravin throughout the cell cycle (Figure 2A, lanes 4 and 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Aurora A, Plk1, and p766-Gravin are concentrated at mitotic spindle poles.
source: Second, conventional immunofluorescent techniques demonstrate that Aurora A (red), Plk1 (green), and p766-Gravin (blue) are concentrated at mitotic spindle poles (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: p-Gravin, Aurora A, and Plk1 decorate a lattice-like structure at mitotic spindle poles reminiscent of pericentriolar material.
source: Third, structured illumination microscopy (SIM, resolution ∼100 nm) revealed that p-Gravin, Aurora A, and Plk1 decorated a higher-order lattice-like structure at mitotic spindle poles reminiscent of pericentriolar material (PCM (Lawo et al., 2012); Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 2D and cited literature.

claim: p766-Gravin/Aurora A sub-complexes are enhanced 3.86-fold during metaphase compared to interphase cells.
source: Quantification of PLA puncta indicated that p766-Gravin/Aurora A sub-complexes was enhanced 3.86-fold during metaphase when compared to interphase cells (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by proximity ligation assay data shown in Figure 2E,F.

claim: The p766-Gravin-Plk1 sub-complex is enriched 10.34-fold during metaphase compared to interphase.
source: The p766-Gravin-Plk1 sub-complex was enriched 10.34-fold (Figure 2G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by proximity ligation assay data shown in Figure 2G,H.

claim: p766-Gravin scaffolds Aurora A with Plk1 at a PCM-like structure on mitotic spindle poles during metaphase.
source: Thus, we conclude that p766-Gravin scaffolds Aurora A with Plk1 at a PCM-like structure on mitotic spindle poles during metaphase.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the combined immunoprecipitation, imaging, and proximity ligation data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Gravin null MEFs exhibit a 3.05-fold reduction in Aurora A at mitotic spindle poles compared to wild-type MEFs.
source: Gravin null MEFs exhibited a loss of p766-Gravin (Figure 3B), a 3.05-fold reduction in Aurora A (Figure 3C), and a 1.87-fold reduction in Plk1 (Figure 3D) when compared to wild-type MEFs.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence signal intensity at spindle poles shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Gravin null MEFs exhibit a 1.87-fold reduction in Plk1 at mitotic spindle poles compared to wild-type MEFs.
source: Gravin null MEFs exhibited a loss of p766-Gravin (Figure 3B), a 3.05-fold reduction in Aurora A (Figure 3C), and a 1.87-fold reduction in Plk1 (Figure 3D) when compared to wild-type MEFs.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence signal intensity at spindle poles shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Signal intensities for the spindle pole marker pericentrin are equivalent in wild-type and Gravin null MEFs.
source: Signal intensities for the spindle pole marker pericentrin were equivalent in cells from both genotypes (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence signal intensity shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Gravin null MEFs show a near complete loss of astral microtubules protruding from spindle poles compared to wild-type controls.
source: Super-resolution analysis by SIM revealed a near complete loss of astral microtubules protruding from the spindle poles of Gravin null MEFs when compared to wild-type controls (Figure 3F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by super-resolution imaging and quantification data shown in Figure 3F,G.

claim: p766-Gravin is unequally distributed between the spindle poles of metaphase cells.
source: Upon closer inspection, we noted that p766-Gravin was unequally distributed between the spindle poles of metaphase cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy imaging shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Components of the Gravin kinase scaffold are selectively enriched at the mother spindle pole.
source: On the basis of signal overlap with the mother centriole marker Cenexin, we were surprised to discover that components of the Gravin kinase scaffold were selectively enriched at this location (Figure 4B,C, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by ground state depletion microscopy data shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: p766-Gravin/Aurora A PLA puncta are 4.16-fold more prevalent at mother spindle poles than at daughter spindle poles.
source: This observation was corroborated by proximity ligation as p766-Gravin/Aurora A PLA puncta were 4.16-fold more prevalent at mother spindle poles than at daughter spindle poles (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by proximity ligation assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,G.

claim: p766-Gravin/Plk1 PLA pairs are enriched 2.35-fold at the mother spindle pole.
source: Likewise, p766-Gravin/Plk1 PLA pairs were enriched 2.35-fold at the mother spindle pole (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by proximity ligation assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Gravin and both kinases (Aurora A and Plk1) are tethered within 20–40 nm of each other at mother spindle poles.
source: Thus, Gravin and both kinases are tethered within 20–40 nm of each other and form a locally anchored signaling complex at mother spindle poles.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on proximity ligation assay data which detects interactions within 40-60 nm.

claim: The location of Plk1 changes upon shRNA-mediated gene silencing of Gravin, with Plk1 now predominating at the daughter spindle pole.
source: Surprisingly, the location of Plk1 changed upon shRNA-mediated gene silencing of Gravin (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H). Plk1 now predominated at the daughter spindle pole (Figure 4E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by ground state depletion microscopy data shown in Figure 4D,E,F.

claim: Ablation of Gravin in tissue culture cell lines instigates the displacement of Aurora A and Plk1 from the spindle pole but may not affect the cellular levels of each enzyme.
source: Additional control experiments in HEK293 cells revealed that cellular levels of both kinases were unaltered in absence of Gravin (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H). This latter observation argues that ablation of Gravin in tissue culture cell lines instigates the displacement of both kinases from the spindle pole but may not affect the cellular levels of each enzyme.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1H and inference from the data.

claim: Astral microtubules protruding from the mother spindle pole are longer than those emanating from the daughter spindle pole in wild-type MEFs.
source: However, upon quantification of three-dimensional (3D) reconstructed SIM images, it was evident that astral microtubules protruding from the mother spindle pool were longer than those emanating from the daughter spindle pole (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: In Gravin null MEFs, the length of astral microtubules protruding from the mother spindle pole is reduced.
source: Notably in Gravin null MEFs, the length of astral microtubules protruding from the mother spindle pool was reduced (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Gravin or elements of its signaling scaffold contribute to the assembly of astral microtubules.
source: Therefore, on the basis of these findings, we can propose that Gravin or elements of its signaling scaffold contribute to the assembly of astral microtubules.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the astral microtubule length data from wild-type and Gravin null MEFs.

claim: Gravin-mediated anchoring of Plk1 to the mother spindle pole contributes to the assembly or maintenance of astral microtubules.
source: Nonetheless, we contend that Gravin-mediated anchoring of Plk1 to the mother spindle pole contributes to the assembly or maintenance of astral microtubules.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on rescue experiments with Gravin T766A mutant and astral microtubule measurements.

claim: Aurora A/Plk1 PLA signal is reduced 1.77-fold upon shRNA depletion of Gravin.
source: Importantly, a 1.77-fold reduction in the PLA signal was measured upon shRNA depletion of Gravin (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by proximity ligation assay quantification shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Gravin is necessary to co-localize Aurora A and Plk1.
source: Importantly, a 1.77-fold reduction in the PLA signal was measured upon shRNA depletion of Gravin (Figure 5B). This implies that Gravin is necessary to co-localize both kinases.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the reduction in Aurora A/Plk1 PLA signal upon Gravin depletion.

claim: Incubation with VX-680 reduced Kemptide phosphorylation by 33.5% in Gravin immune complexes.
source: Aurora A kinase activity was defined as the number of counts (cpm x 103/IP) blocked by the inhibitor drug VX-680 (Tyler et al., 2014). Incubation with VX-680 reduced Kemptide phosphorylation by 33.5% (Figure 5C, n = 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figure 5C and cited literature.

claim: Gravin-depletion results in a twofold reduction in p288-Aurora A and p210-Plk1 signals in mitotic lysates.
source: Gravin-depletion resulted in a twofold reduction in the p288-Aurora A and p210-Plk1 signals as detected by immunoblot (Figure 5D lane 4, Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot and densitometry data shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: Gravin constrains active Aurora A and Plk1 to facilitate signal relay from one kinase to the next.
source: Collectively, these experiments indicate that Gravin constrains active Aurora A and Plk1 to facilitate signal relay from one kinase to the next (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the kinase activity assays and phospho-kinase detection experiments.

claim: A central region of Gravin (amino acids 451 to 900) directly interacts with Aurora A.
source: In vitro binding studies using purified GST-Gravin fragments mapped a central region of the anchoring protein (amino acids 451 to 900) that directly interacts with Aurora A (Figure 6A top panel, lane 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Expression of the Aurora A disruptor causes a mitotic delay (mean time 85.17 ± 3.77 min, n = 55) compared to control cells (64.57 ± 4.09 min, n = 95).
source: Expression of the Aurora A disruptor caused a mitotic delay (mean time 85.17 ± 3.77 min, n = 55) when compared to control cells (64.57 ± 4.09 min, n = 95; Figure 6C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging time-course data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: Correct targeting of Aurora A facilitates efficient mitosis.
source: Thus, correct targeting of Aurora A facilitates efficient mitosis.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the mitotic delay observed when Aurora A is displaced from Gravin.

claim: Metaphase is delayed in Gravin shRNA depleted cells (78.04 ± 3.06 min, n = 29) compared to control (45.86 ± 1.27 min, n = 28).
source: Metaphase was delayed in Gravin shRNA depleted cells (78.04 ± 3.06 min, n = 29) compared to control (45.86 ± 1.27 min, n = 28, Figure 6E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging time-course data shown in Figure 6E,F.

claim: Rescue with murine Gravin corrects the mitotic delay defect in Gravin-depleted cells (57.41 ± 3.63 min n = 37).
source: This defect was corrected upon rescue with murine Gravin (57.41 ± 3.63 min n = 37; Figure 6E–G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging time-course data shown in Figure 6E-G.

claim: Rescue with Gravin T766A, a Plk1-binding defective mutant, is unable to restore normal mitotic progression (90.32 ± 6.33 min, n = 31).
source: In contrast, rescue with Gravin T766A, a Plk1-binding defective mutant, was unable to restore normal mitotic progression (90.32 ± 6.33 min, n = 31; Figure 6E,F,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging time-course data shown in Figure 6E,F,H.

claim: A GravinΔPKA mutant that cannot anchor PKA restores normal cell cycle progression (55.69 ± 3.41 min, n = 29).
source: Experiments with a GravinΔPKA mutant that cannot anchor PKA (Nauert et al., 1997) restored normal cell cycle progression, thereby excluding a role for Gravin-associated-PKA in this process (55.69 ± 3.41 min, n = 29; Figure 6E,F,I).
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging time-course data shown in Figure 6E,F,I and cited literature.

claim: Aurora A proximity to Plk1 facilitated by Gravin promotes efficient mitotic progression.
source: Collectively, these studies propose a mechanism where Aurora A proximity to Plk1 facilitates efficient mitotic progression, as both kinases are constrained by Gravin.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the rescue experiments with Gravin mutants and their effects on mitotic timing.

claim: Ectopic expression of the Aurora A disruptor promotes a 20° misalignment of the mitotic spindle compared to control cells.
source: Ectopic expression of the Aurora A disruptor perturbed spindle orientation. Mislocalization of Aurora A promoted a 20° misalignment of the mitotic spindle when compared to control cells transfected with empty vector (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by spindle angle measurements shown in Figure 7B,C.

claim: In Gravin-depleted cells, the perturbation of spindle orientation is 40°.
source: Yet in Gravin-depleted cells, the perturbation of spindle orientation was 40° (Figure 7D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by spindle angle measurements shown in Figure 7D,E.

claim: Spindle angle defects in Gravin-depleted cells are rescued upon expression of the mouse Gravin ortholog.
source: Notably, these more severe spindle angle defects were rescued upon expression of the mouse Gravin ortholog (Figure 7D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by spindle angle measurements shown in Figure 7D,E.

claim: Spindle angle defects are only partially rescued upon expression of the Plk1-binding defective Gravin T766A mutant (angles averaging around 20°).
source: In contrast, spindle angle defects were only partially rescued upon expression of the Plk1-binding defective Gravin T766A mutant (angles averaging around 20°; Figure 7D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by spindle angle measurements shown in Figure 7D,E.

claim: Abnormal orientation and positioning of mitotic spindles are observed in Gravin null MEFs.
source: In contrast, abnormal orientation and positioning of mitotic spindles were observed in Gravin null MEFs (Figure 7G and Video 2, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D reconstructed confocal imaging shown in Figure 7G and Video 2.

claim: Gravin, through its interaction with Aurora A and Plk1, ensures correct spindle orientation during mitosis.
source: Thus, we propose that Gravin, through its interaction with Aurora A and Plk1, ensures correct spindle orientation during mitosis.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the spindle orientation defects observed when Gravin or its kinase interactions are disrupted.

claim: The cellular layering of seminiferous tubules and lumenal organization of spermatids are disrupted in Gravin knockout mice.
source: In contrast, the cellular layering of seminiferous tubules and lumenal organization of spermatids are disrupted in Gravin knockout mice (Figure 8B,C; right).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging of tissue sections shown in Figure 8B,C.

claim: The diameter of the lumen is significantly decreased in seminiferous tubules from Gravin knockout mice.
source: Of note, the diameter of the lumen is significantly decreased in seminiferous tubules from Gravin knockout mice (Figure 8D).
evidence: The claim is supported by lumen diameter measurements shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Elongating spermatids are haphazardly dispersed throughout the lumen in Gravin knockout mice.
source: In addition, the elongating spermatids are haphazardly dispersed throughout the lumen (Figure 8C, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Morphological changes in seminiferous tubules are a consequence of abnormal spindle orientation within dividing germ line stem cells.
source: We postulate that both morphological changes are a consequence of abnormal spindle orientation within dividing germ line stem cells.
evidence: The claim is speculation based on the observed morphological changes and spindle orientation defects.

claim: Mitotic Gravin knockout germ line stem cells display randomized mitotic spindle orientation (average angle of 47.67°, n = 98).
source: Importantly, this increased incidence of spindle angle randomization was evident in mitotic Gravin knockout germ line stem cells (average angle of 47.67°, n = 98; Figure 8H).
evidence: The claim is supported by spindle angle measurements in tissue sections shown in Figure 8H.

claim: The spindle misorientation phenotype observed in vivo is a consequence of displacing Plk1 from mitotic spindle poles.
source: On the basis of our cell-based and biochemical studies in Figures 3, 4, we postulated that the spindle misorientation phenotype observed in vivo is a consequence of displacing Plk1 from mitotic spindle poles.
evidence: The claim is speculation based on the cell-based and biochemical studies showing Plk1 displacement.

claim: In wild-type seminiferous tubule sections, the Plk1 signal is prominent at mitotic spindle poles.
source: In wild-type sections, the Plk1 signal was prominent at mitotic spindle poles (Figure 8I, top mid panel; green).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 8I.

claim: In Gravin knockout sections, the Plk1 signal is more disperse.
source: Conversely, in Gravin knockout sections, the Plk1 signal was more disperse (Figure 8I, lower mid panel; green).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 8I.

claim: Line scan analysis detected an asymmetric distribution of Plk1 at one spindle pole in wild-type cells.
source: Line scan analysis detected an asymmetric distribution of Plk1 at one spindle pole in wild-type cells (Figure 8K, top panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by line scan analysis shown in Figure 8K.

claim: A more uniform distribution of Plk1 was detected in Gravin knockout cells.
source: Conversely, a more uniform distribution of this kinase was detected in Gravin knockout cells (Figure 8K, lower panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by line scan analysis shown in Figure 8K.

claim: Gravin functions to preferentially anchor Plk1 at one spindle pole in vivo.
source: Quantitative analysis of multiple cells confirmed these findings further suggesting that Gravin functions to preferentially anchor Plk1 at one spindle pole in vivo (Figure 8L).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the quantitative analysis of Plk1 distribution shown in Figure 8L.

claim: A 3.82-fold increase in Oct3/4-positive cells is observed in Gravin knockout seminiferous tubule sections.
source: A 3.82-fold increase in Oct3/4-positive cells was observed in Gravin knockout sections (n = 4; Figure 8M,N).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of Oct3/4-positive cells shown in Figure 8M,N.

claim: Randomized spindle angles and the concomitant over-proliferation of germ line stem cells may underlie the pathological abnormalities observed in Gravin knockout seminiferous tubule organization as well as human seminoma.
source: Thus, randomized spindle angles and the concomitant over-proliferation of germ line stem cells may underlie the pathological abnormalities observed in Gravin knockout seminiferous tubule organization as well as human seminoma (Figures 1, 8).
evidence: The claim is speculation based on the observed spindle angle defects and stem cell proliferation data.

claim: Aurora A and Plk1 act together to promote spindle pole maturation.
source: Aurora A and Plk1 are two kinases generally considered to act together to promote spindle pole maturation (Hannak et al., 2001; Soung et al., 2009; Lee and Rhee, 2011; Joukov et al., 2014; Kong et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Aurora A and Plk1 have an additional role in the establishment of spindle orientation during mitotic progression.
source: We have discovered an additional role for both kinases in the establishment of spindle orientation during mitotic progression.
evidence: The claim is based on the data presented in the manuscript showing spindle orientation defects when the Gravin-Aurora A-Plk1 complex is disrupted.

claim: Both active Aurora A and Plk1 must be associated with Gravin to establish spindle orientation.
source: A key element of our finding is that both active kinases must be associated with the scaffolding protein Gravin to fulfill this ancillary function.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the rescue experiments showing that disrupting Gravin's interaction with either kinase impairs spindle orientation.

claim: Formation of a Gravin-Aurora A-Plk1 scaffold at the mother spindle pole may facilitate signal relay to drive spatial and temporal phosphorylation of mitotic substrates.
source: Formation of a Gravin-Aurora A-Plk1 scaffold at this location may facilitate signal relay as depicted in Figure 5F to drive the spatial and temporal phosphorylation pattern of as yet unknown mitotic substrates.
evidence: The claim is speculation about the function of the scaffold based on the observed kinase activities and localization.

claim: Clustering of Aurora A and Plk1 at the mother spindle pole coordinates the assembly of astral microtubules that orient the mitotic spindle.
source: Clustering of these enzymes at this location can either catalyze the efficient assembly of the PCM or alternatively coordinate the assembly of astral microtubules that orient the mitotic spindle. The super-resolution imaging analysis of Gravin null MEFs in Figure 3F argues strongly for the latter as these cells are deficient in astral microtubules but contain equal amounts of a canonical PCM protein, pericentrin ((Doxsey et al., 1994); Figure 3E,G).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that Gravin null cells have normal pericentrin but reduced astral microtubules.

claim: Gravin-mediated clustering of Aurora A and Plk1 at the mother spindle pole provides a means to more precisely regulate symmetric cell division.
source: One new concept that emerges from our studies is that Gravin-mediated clustering of Aurora A and Plk1 at the mother spindle pole provides a means to more precisely regulate symmetric cell division.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the combined data showing effects on astral microtubules, spindle orientation, and symmetric division.

claim: Loss of Gravin impacts the protrusion of astral microtubules.
source: First, data presented in Figure 3F,G indicate that loss of Gravin impacts the protrusion of astral microtubules.
evidence: The claim is supported by super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 3F,G.

claim: Symmetric cell division is lost in Gravin null MEFs.
source: Second, data presented in Figure 8 show that symmetric cell division is lost in Gravin null MEFs.
evidence: The claim is supported by spindle orientation measurements in tissue sections shown in Figure 8.

claim: Sequestering Aurora A and Plk1 at the mother spindle pole ensures that each kinase is optimally positioned to regulate astral microtubule protrusion.
source: Moreover, we postulate that the sequestering these enzymes at the mother spindle pole ensures that each kinase is optimally positioned to play a role in the regulation of astral microtubule protrusion, a process that influences the correct orientation of mitotic spindles during cell division.
evidence: The claim is speculation based on the observed localization and functional data.

claim: Signaling events downstream of Plk1 modulate the correct orientation of mitotic spindles.
source: This mechanism is compatible with two recent reports indicating that signaling events downstream Plk1 modulate the correct orientation mitotic spindles (Hanafusa et al., 2015; Yan et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: Gravin functions as the anchor for Aurora A and Plk1 at the mother spindle pole.
source: However, a vital new piece of this puzzle, uncovered solely from our work, is that Gravin functions as the anchor for these enzymes.
evidence: The claim is based on the biochemical and imaging data showing Gravin's interaction with and localization of both kinases.

claim: The orientation of the mitotic spindle influences cell fate determination and tissue organization.
source: Another theme emerging from the data in Figure 8 is that the orientation of the mitotic spindle becomes increasingly important during stem cell division. These events influence cell fate determination and tissue organization (Siller and Doe, 2009; Gillies and Cabernard, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature and the data in Figure 8.

claim: Gravin knockout mice exhibit an increase in Oct3/4, a marker for stem cells within the seminiferous tubule.
source: In keeping with this notion, Gravin knockout mice exhibit an increase in Oct3/4, a marker for stem cells within the seminiferous tubule (Figure 8M,N).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of Oct3/4-positive cells shown in Figure 8M,N.

claim: Clinical studies detect a marked increase in Oct3/4-positive cells in solid-state tumors including seminoma.
source: This is evocative of clinical studies that detect a marked increase in Oct3/4-positive cells in solid-state tumors including seminoma (Singh et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior clinical literature.

claim: Abnormalities in Gravin expression that promote mislocalization of Aurora A and Plk1 contribute to defects in orientation of mitotic spindles to potentiate seminoma progression.
source: Therefore, we postulate that abnormalities in Gravin expression that promote mislocalization of Aurora A and Plk1 contributes to defects in orientation of mitotic spindles to potentiate seminoma progression.
evidence: The claim is speculation based on the combined observations in human seminoma samples and mouse models.

claim: Gravin knockout mice do not develop seminomas.
source: However, Gravin knockout mice do not develop seminomas, yet some of the aforementioned abnormalities are evident in these animals.
evidence: The claim is an observation about the phenotype of Gravin knockout mice.

claim: Gravin knockout mice have difficulty breeding and upon aging display a tendency to develop prostate hyperplasia.
source: For example, these animals have difficultly breeding and upon aging display a tendency to develop prostate hyperplasia (Akakura et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior literature on Gravin knockout mice.

claim: Perturbation of Gravin-mediated signaling events during mitosis may promote a chronic decrease in organization of the seminiferous tubules with concomitant impairment of reproductive viability.
source: Therefore, we speculate that perturbation of Gravin-mediated signaling events during mitosis may promote a chronic decrease in organization of the seminiferous tubules with concomitant impairment of reproductive viability.
evidence: The claim is speculation based on the observed phenotypes in Gravin knockout mice.

claim: Gravin constrains Aurora A and Plk1 in an asymmetric manner to control spindle orientation during mitosis.
source: Finally, when the mouse studies are considered in the context of our biochemical analysis and imaging of clinical samples, we can conclude that Gravin constrains Aurora A and Plk1 in an asymmetric manner to control spindle orientation during mitosis.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the combined data from mouse models, cell culture, and human samples.

claim: A new macromolecular signaling scaffold drives stem cell maintenance and cell differentiation in seminiferous tubules.
source: Thus, we identify and define a new macromolecular signaling scaffold that drives stem cell maintenance and cell differentiation in seminiferous tubules.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the combined data showing the role of the Gravin-Aurora A-Plk1 complex in spindle orientation and stem cell division.

claim: Phosphorylation of Gravin on Threonine 766 promotes recruitment of Plk1.
source: Phosphorylation of Gravin on Threonine 766 promotes recruitment of Plk1, a kinase that prompts mitotic progression and appropriate spindle formation (Canton et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Mutation or amplification of Gravin has been linked to melanoma, prostate, and ovarian cancers.
source: Mutation or amplification of Gravin has been linked to melanoma, prostate, and ovarian cancers, yet nothing is known about the role of this kinase-anchoring protein in solid tumors (Xia et al., 2001; Bateman et al., 2015; Finger et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Testicular germ line tumors are the most frequently diagnosed solid cancers in men aged 15–40 years.
source: Testicular germ line tumors are the most frequently diagnosed solid cancers in men aged 15–40 years.
evidence: The claim is based on established medical knowledge.

claim: Currently, 200,000 men develop seminoma annually.
source: Currently, 200,000 men develop seminoma annually (Fung et al., 2007; Burum-Auensen et al., 2010; Singh et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to epidemiological literature.

claim: Correct orientation of the mitotic spindle in stem cells underlies organogenesis.
source: Correct orientation of the mitotic spindle in stem cells underlies organogenesis.
evidence: The claim is based on established biological knowledge.

claim: Spindle abnormalities correlate with cancer progression in germ line-derived tumors.
source: Spindle abnormalities correlate with cancer progression in germ line-derived tumors.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about cancer biology.

claim: Depletion of Gravin correlates with an increased mitotic index and disorganization of seminiferous tubules.
source: Depletion of Gravin correlates with an increased mitotic index and disorganization of seminiferous tubules.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from human seminoma samples and mouse knockout models shown in Figure 1.

claim: The Gravin scaffold accumulates at the mother spindle pole during metaphase.
source: Biochemical, super-resolution imaging, and enzymology approaches establish that this Gravin scaffold accumulates at the mother spindle pole during metaphase.
evidence: The claim is supported by biochemical, imaging, and enzymology data shown in Figures 2-5.

claim: Manipulating elements of the Gravin-Aurora A-Plk1 axis prompts mitotic delay and prevents appropriate assembly of astral microtubules to promote spindle misorientation.
source: Manipulating elements of the Gravin-Aurora A-Plk1 axis prompts mitotic delay and prevents appropriate assembly of astral microtubules to promote spindle misorientation.
evidence: The claim is supported by live-cell imaging, super-resolution imaging, and spindle angle measurements shown in Figures 3, 6, and 7.

claim: An overabundance of Oct3/4 positive germ line stem cells displays randomized orientation of mitotic spindles in seminiferous tubules from Gravin−/− mice.
source: These pathological responses are conserved in seminiferous tubules from Gravin−/− mice where an overabundance of Oct3/4 positive germ line stem cells displays randomized orientation of mitotic spindles.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence and spindle angle measurements in mouse tissue sections shown in Figure 8.

claim: Gravin-mediated recruitment of Aurora A and Plk1 to the mother (oldest) spindle pole contributes to the fidelity of symmetric cell division.
source: Thus, we propose that Gravin-mediated recruitment of Aurora A and Plk1 to the mother (oldest) spindle pole contributes to the fidelity of symmetric cell division.
evidence: The claim is a proposal based on the combined data showing localization, function, and phenotypes.

claim: Mitotic cell division relies heavily on the spatial and temporal synchronization of protein kinase activity at the mitotic spindle.
source: This process relies heavily on the spatial and temporal synchronization of protein kinase activity at the mitotic spindle, a macromolecular machine that segregates the chromosomes and guides them towards the daughter cells (Lowery et al., 2004; Nigg and Stearns, 2011; Langeberg and Scott, 2015).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Correct orientation of the mitotic spindle during cell division combined with local kinase signaling is crucial for cell fate determination, tissue organization, and development.
source: Correct orientation of the mitotic spindle during cell division combined with local kinase signaling is crucial for cell fate determination, tissue organization, and development (Yamashita et al., 2007; Lesage et al., 2010; Gillies and Cabernard, 2011; Kiyomitsu and Cheeseman, 2012; Pelletier and Yamashita, 2012; Joukov et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The mother spindle pole contains the oldest centriole and remains anchored near the stem-cell niche.
source: The mother spindle pole contains the oldest centriole and remains anchored near the stem-cell niche, while the daughter spindle pole migrates to the opposite side of the cell to complete spindle formation (Yamashita et al., 2007; Izumi and Kaneko, 2012).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: A spindle orientation complex has been identified at the mother spindle pole containing protein components that promote maturation.
source: Recently, a spindle orientation complex has been identified at the mother spindle pole containing protein components that promote maturation (Yamashita et al., 2007; Izumi and Kaneko, 2012; Chen et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Loss of disease-linked genes encoding spindle orientation proteins causes mitotic delays and spindle misorientation phenotypes.
source: Several disease-linked genes encode these proteins and their loss causes mitotic delays and spindle misorientation phenotypes (Buchman et al., 2010; Gruber et al., 2011; Tan et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2014; Kim and Rhee, 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Spindle orientation defects that promote an imbalance between symmetric and asymmetric cell divisions have been implicated in the progression of germ line-derived cancers such as teratomas, seminomas, and ovarian carcinomas.
source: Spindle orientation defects that promote an imbalance between symmetric and asymmetric cell divisions have been implicated in the progression of germ line-derived cancers such as teratomas, seminomas, and ovarian carcinomas (Neumüller and Knoblich, 2009).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Germ line-derived cancers can be exacerbated by mislocalization or misregulation of mitogenic and mitotic protein kinase cascades.
source: These cancers can be exacerbated by mislocalization or misregulation of mitogenic and mitotic protein kinase cascades (Carnegie et al., 2009; Scott and Pawson, 2009).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Gravin/AKAP12/SSeCKS has been implicated in the control of mitotic progression.
source: The A-kinase anchoring protein Gravin/AKAP12/SSeCKS has been implicated in the control of mitotic progression (Xia et al., 2001; Gelman, 2010; Canton et al., 2012; Canton and Scott, 2013).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Gravin is required to spatially coordinate the activities of Aurora A and polo-like kinase 1 (Plk1).
source: Mechanistic studies show that Gravin is required to spatially coordinate the activities of Aurora A and polo-like kinase 1 (Plk1), two kinases that act in concert to promote spindle orientation.
evidence: The claim is supported by the mechanistic studies presented in the manuscript.
